ActualTransport: IPv4 loopback TCP endpoints in one console process
Scope: The actual selection/product coordinator now maps each fixed positive employee product once using immutable raw inputs and explicit frozen count modes. Each returned scalar is retained before source/ledger postguards; partial failures remain unknown without repeated lookup or exchange. Complete results publish atomically, preserve raw capture grade/count/weight/fingerprints, and generate CLR candidate return plans without binding or permissions. Typed native GetItems/GetIngredients/direct-field/count primitives compile; a separate owner retains up to seventeen explicit references plus the original managed bridge/ledger/selection. Source release requires MappingReady and mapping exit; return release requires all matching product plans SaveConfirmed and never retries unknown free. All 267 Core/TCP tests actually ran with eleven new synthetic mapping fixtures. Native-only managed owner retention changed after Core validation; all 84 actual Core source inputs stayed identical and final warning-as-error plugin compilation used a fresh 141-input seal. One new private offline metadata report covers four types, two lookup declarations, two pointer constructors and five direct Int32 proxies. One new PE analysis covers one count-helper known range with 48 instructions/7 direct edges/zero indirect calls, without proving full method/formula semantics. No native call/handle execution, category/count-mode producer, final-grade policy, mapping equivalence, capture diversion, inventory delta/save, guest isolation, host world adoption, dual-game normal return or cold configuration is verified. Full M3-M7 remains required.
